title: The Wild Oath
premise: When the crown of Thornfell declares a kingdom-wide hunt for anyone bearing the old gift, runaway apprentice Theo Dunmore discovers his late mistress bound her own magic into his memory to hide him—and the binding is killing him. Fleeing through the smuggler's roads he knows best, Theo falls in with a disgraced royal physician who reveals the truth: the king is not the king, but a hollowed vessel worn by an oath-eating entity that feeds on gifted minds, and Theo's stolen memories are the key to unbinding it. To save himself and the realm, Theo must surrender the memories that make him who he is, trading his past for the kingdom's future. In the end he unbinds the king at terrible cost, waking with a stranger's face in his mind and a single scar where his name used to be.
about_author: W. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. Their work blends folklore, treacherous landscapes, and characters who survive by knowing when to run.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In the mountain village of Hollowmere, Theo burns his mistress's grimoire page by page to hide his gift, mourning the old hedge-witch who died protecting him. When crown riders arrive posting the Proclamation of the Hunt, his carefully buried magic flares unbidden, lighting every lantern in the square. Fear and grief collide; he flees into the Thornfell passes that same night.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Navigating a frozen smuggler's road, Theo trades a charm of warmth to a caravan master for passage, calculating survival like coin. He reflects on the mistress's last words—remember nothing, forget nothing—and the headaches that have plagued him since her death. The beat is wary competence shadowed by dread as he realizes the binding in his mind is unraveling.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, shifting briefly to the physician Maren. Theo is ambushed by a bounty-taker who can smell the gift; Maren, a disgraced royal physician fleeing the capital, kills the hunter to save him. She recognizes the binding's signature in his eyes. The emotional beat is reluctant alliance—two people who trusted no one, now bound by shared danger.

chapters.title: The Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. In a waystation, Maren reveals what she fled: the king has not slept in three years, his shadow moves wrong, and everyone who tends him forgets his face by morning. She believes an oath-eater—a thing that devours gifted minds—wears him. Theo's stolen memories may be the counter-oath. The beat is horror dawning into terrible purpose.

chapters.title: Debts Written in Skin
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Maren attempts a diagnostic rite; it tears open a sealed memory—Theo's mother, burned as a gift-bearer when he was six. The binding his mistress placed is not protection but a cage, and it is consuming him to keep the oath-eater from finding his mind. Grief and rage surface; he nearly walks away. The beat is the first crack in his self-deception.

chapters.title: Thornfell's Teeth
chapters.summary: Theo and Maren, alternating. A rockslide—no accident—cuts the pass; crown wardens with gift-hunting hounds close in. Theo uses his knowledge of smuggler routes to lead them through a collapsing mine, but the effort burns magic he cannot spare, and his memories begin skipping like a scratched record. The beat is survival at mounting cost.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. They shelter with Sera, a blind mapmaker whose father charted the old oath-stones. Sera reveals the oath-eater was bound centuries ago beneath the capital by a circle of witches—Theo's mistress among their last heirs. The binding Theo carries is a piece of that great seal. Hope kindles, and with it the weight of destiny Theo never asked for.

chapters.title: A Market of Small Magics
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In the free-town of Gallow's Rest, Theo buys a memory-anchor charm from a fence of enchanted goods—and is recognized by an old fellow apprentice, Ilsa, now a crown informant. She hesitates before betraying him, torn between survival and old loyalty. The beat is the corrupting arithmetic of the hunt: everyone is pricing everyone.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ilsa sells his location anyway, and wardens take Maren captive while Theo escapes by burning a memory of his mother's face to fuel a concealment working. He wakes not remembering her at all, and understands exactly what the endgame will demand of him. The beat is grief for a loss he cannot even recall.

chapters.title: Cells Beneath the Keep
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. In the capital's dungeons, Maren is brought before the king—and sees the thing behind his eyes recognize her craft. It offers her her old life back if she delivers the last seal-bearer. She plays along, buying time, while discovering the entity's hunger is failing: it needs Theo soon or the crown itself will crumble. The beat is dread sharpened into a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone and fraying, Theo follows the mistress's hidden instructions to the first oath-stone, guided by Sera's maps. Each stone he touches returns a fragment of sealed memory—including the night his mistress bound him, and her whispered apology. He learns she loved him enough to damn him. The beat is forgiveness beginning where anger burns out.

chapters.title: The Second Stone
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the second stone, wardens ambush him; Ilsa, wracked with guilt, turns her coat and fights beside him, taking a mortal wound. Dying, she tells him the informant network is the entity's nervous system—the hunt was never about finding the gifted, but herding the seal-bearers to the capital. The beat is sacrifice and the shattering of Theo's belief that hiding was ever possible.

chapters.title: What Wears the King
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren witnesses the entity feed on a captured gift-child and nearly breaks her cover to intervene. She maps the king's condition from within: the oath-eater is fused to the coronation oath itself—unbinding it may kill the king, or worse, leave the oath vacant for something hungrier. The beat is moral vertigo: every path costs a life.

chapters.title: The Circle's Last Heirs
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, joined by Sera. Theo reaches the third stone, where the ghosts of the original binding circle linger as memory-echoes. They test him: would he trade his past for the realm? He cannot answer, and the stone refuses him. Sera tells him the seal doesn't want a hero—it wants a witness. The beat is humility before an old, patient magic.

chapters.title: Gallows Rest Burns
chapters.summary: Theo and Maren, alternating. Reunited, they return to Gallow's Rest to destroy the informant network and find the crown has burned the free-town as an example. Among the ashes, Theo finds the fence dying, who gives him the memory-anchor charm charged with a single instruction: the fourth stone is beneath the throne itself. The beat is resolve hardened by atrocity.

chapters.title: Entering the Lion's Mouth
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Using Maren's stolen credentials and Ilsa's informant tokens, the pair infiltrate the capital during the king's Feast of the Oath. Theo walks the same halls where his mother was burned, his sealed memories resonating with the stones in the foundations. The beat is terror transmuted into eerie calm—he was always meant to come back.

chapters.title: The Feast of the Oath
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. At the feast, the entity, wearing the king, greets Theo openly before the court—revealing that half the nobles are hollowed vessels already. It offers Theo a bargain: surrender the seal and it will return every memory it has taken, including his mother's face. The beat is temptation at its most exquisite, and Theo's quiet refusal.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Captured and bound to the fourth stone beneath the throne, Theo begins the counter-oath as the entity tears at his mind. Maren and Sera hold the ritual's outer circle while the entity floods him with every memory it has eaten—a kingdom's worth of stolen lives. The beat is the climax: Theo pouring himself out, memory by memory, into the seal.

chapters.title: The Empty Throne
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The entity, unbound, tries to seize the vacant oath—and finds Theo has filled the seal with something it cannot digest: ordinary, stubborn human memory, unglamorous and endless. It unravels. The king collapses, mortal and dying but finally his own. The beat is triumph laced with horror at the price still being paid.

chapters.title: What Theo Paid
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, fragmented. Theo wakes in the physician's ward with most of his life gone—his mistress, his mother, his years on the road, all mist. Only the anchor charm holds one thread: the feel of the mountain passes under his boots. He cannot remember why he fought, only that he won. The beat is desolation and the question of what remains when memory is gone.

chapters.title: The Kingdom of Small Things
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The Proclamation is rescinded; gifted folk emerge from hiding. Sera begins mapping the freed oath-stones, Maren rebuilds the physician's college, and the dying king names a council instead of an heir, distrusting any single crown. Theo watches from the edges, a stranger to his own victory. The beat is cautious, imperfect hope taking root.

chapters.title: The Wild Oath
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the anniversary, Theo walks the smuggler's roads again, body remembering what his mind cannot. At the first oath-stone, the circle's echo returns one gift unasked: not his memories, but a single new one—the sound of his mother's voice saying his name. He weeps, laughs, and walks on, carrying a past he chose rather than one he was given. The beat is bittersweet peace: survival was never free, but it was worth the price.
